visual_goal: Show the Adyen account tree: one company account, a Stayloft account group, three merchant accounts split by entity, perimeter and payout currency, each paying out to its entity's safeguarding vault and each landing in its own clearing account.
prompt: A top-down tree diagram. At the top, a plain office building labeled 'Northmere Group'. One line down to a folder labeled 'Stayloft'. From the folder three lines fan down to three merchant-account boxes in a row, left to right: 'EEA account', 'INTL account', 'UK account'. Below the boxes, two vaults: a blue vault on the left labeled 'Safeguarding B.V.' and a teal vault on the right labeled 'Safeguarding UK'. Thick green coin-pipe arrows: one from 'EEA account' into 'Safeguarding B.V.', one from 'INTL account' into 'Safeguarding B.V.', and one from 'UK account' into 'Safeguarding UK'. Beside each of the three merchant-account boxes, a small open book labeled 'Clearing', each with its own thin dotted arrow from its merchant-account box carrying a small report document, so each box has its own book. Exactly six arrows plus four tree lines.
alt: A tree from the Northmere Group company account to the Stayloft account group and three merchant accounts, EEA, INTL and UK; EEA and INTL pay out to the B.V. safeguarding vault and UK to the UK vault, and each merchant account has its own clearing book.

visual_goal: Show that for the Lisbon payment the API response gives identity, webhooks give operational state and the settlement report gives money, and that each becomes a canonical event reaching SFP.
prompt: A left-to-right diagram. On the left, a box labeled 'Northmere Pay'. On the right, a plain office building labeled 'Adyen'. One arrow at the top runs from 'Northmere Pay' right into 'Adyen'. Below it, three return arrows run from 'Adyen' back left into 'Northmere Pay', stacked one above the other, all three with their arrowheads touching 'Northmere Pay'; each carries a different object: the upper return arrow carries a small blank tag labeled 'API response' with the word 'identity' beside it; the middle return arrow carries a lightning bolt labeled 'Webhooks' with the word 'state' beside it; the lower return arrow carries a document with a few plain coins labeled 'Settlement report' with the word 'money' beside it. Below 'Northmere Pay', a conveyor belt carrying small blank event cards; the words 'Canonical events' are written once, under the belt. One arrow from 'Northmere Pay' down onto the belt, and one arrow from the right end of the belt into an open book labeled 'SFP'. Exactly six arrows.
alt: A traveler pays through Northmere Pay to Adyen; three returns come back: the API response gives identity, webhooks give state and the settlement report gives money, and Northmere Pay turns them into canonical events on a conveyor into the SFP subledger.

visual_goal: Show the two Adyen feeds doing two jobs: webhooks carry operational state through a receiver and an idempotent consumer, reports carry money and fees; both become canonical events, and BlackLine matches subledger, report and bank.
prompt: A left-to-right diagram with two horizontal lanes. At the far left, a plain office building labeled 'Adyen'. Upper lane: one arrow with a lightning bolt labeled 'webhooks' from 'Adyen' into a box with a shield labeled 'Receiver', then one arrow into a box with a filter labeled 'Idempotent consumer', then one arrow into a stack of blank event cards with the words 'Canonical events' written once above the stack. Lower lane: one arrow labeled 'reports' carrying a document with a few plain coins from 'Adyen' into a box labeled 'Report loader', then one arrow from 'Report loader' up into the 'Canonical events' stack. From 'Canonical events' one arrow right into an open book labeled 'SFP'. At the lower right, a box with three interlocking puzzle pieces labeled 'BlackLine', receiving three arrows: one from 'SFP', one from 'Report loader', and one from a single bank building labeled 'Bank' that sits at the bottom, directly below 'Report loader'. There is only one bank building in the picture. Exactly nine arrows.
alt: Adyen webhooks pass a receiver and an idempotent consumer, and Adyen reports pass a report loader; both become canonical events feeding the SFP subledger, and BlackLine matches SFP, the report and the bank.
